# Tasks ready to build

It is command-only: type `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`. Every run rewrites `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md`.

a named spec is `<interpreter> -X utf8 scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`, and `--recommend` names `docs/specs/<slug>`.

## First prompt

```text
/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build
@docs/specs/<slug>/
```

Leave out the folder to check every slice under `docs/specs/`.

The rest is the same scope, including a slice such as `cc 1.0`:

```text
/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build build-map cc 1.0
```

## What it checks

| Check | Where it lands |
| --- | --- |
| Ticked in `tasks.md` | **Done** when `verify.md` lists it as verified, otherwise **Needs verify** |
| `plan.md` missing | Blocked |
| A kept-open question in `spec.md` | **Waiting on a question** when its `Blocks:` line names the task (recorded). `Blocks: none` blocks no task (recorded). `Blocks: whole slice` holds every unfinished task (recorded) and the line says Holds the whole slice. With no `Blocks:` line, the question holds the `T#` ids named in its text (inferred from the text), and holds the whole slice only when no task is named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded (1.137.0). Who comes from "Waiting for", then the latest Pending or Asked line; with neither, the line says Nobody is named to answer it yet (1.170.0). A plan Risk that says do not implement until resolved is **Blocked** when it matches no question, or matches a question with no `Blocks:` line and no inferred tasks. It matches on the question's first sentence, a `(question: <first words>)` tag, or the same Blocks tasks named in the risk. The line wins |
| An `## Approval needed` item with no matching `Approved:` line (1.141.0) | **Waiting** on that person, for the tasks on `Holds:`. Other tasks still start (`ready-partial`). A matching `Approved:` line clears the hold. The task is not ticked here |
| Tasks it waits on | **Waits in order** while a real earlier task is unticked (recorded from `(after: T#)`, or inferred from the task just before it). A cycle, or an `(after:)` that names no task, is **Blocked**. A task on a branch caught in a loop is **Blocked** in the counts and the map, with a `Loop:` line (1.154.0) |
| Otherwise | **Ready**. When `plan.md` has no `Reviewed:` line, it adds a warning to run `/crav1-review-plan` (inferred). When the review still has open `P#`s, it says so |
| Waits on a held task | **Waiting** too, reason `held, waits on T3` (1.132.0). Who is the person on the question that started the hold |

The result line is `ready`, `ready-partial`, or `not-ready`. `ready-partial` means some tasks can start now and some are held. `not-ready` means nothing can start. A cycle, a missing task, no plan, Needs verify, or a plan-review warning still records `not-ready`. The walk record stays `Result: ready-partial`. `/crav1-build-tasks` starts the ready tasks and refuses a held task with its reason.

The branch is the name `scripts/build_map.py docs/specs/<slug> --recommend T#` prints. A task is shown as `T#` plus its short name, the same words as the Tasks field in `build-map.md`. A held task names the open question and who has it, or `held, waits on T3`. The bottom keeps Waiting lines and the one line `/crav1-build-tasks builds one task without the walk.`, with no `Next:` line.

For a slice where T7 waits on T2, T3 and T6 on T7, T4 on T3 and T7, and T5 on T4, the order is T1 → T2 → T7 → T3 | T6 → T4 → T5. `/crav1-build-tasks`, `/crav1-build-features` and `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec` use that order.

## What you see

the script prints the whole reply and the assistant gives it once as the answer, as-is, with at most one short lead sentence and without first pasting the raw tool output: `walk_progress.py readiness --root <spec-folder> --write-map --text`. a not-ready ending starts with `Run next:` naming the first real next step.

```text
Tasks ready to build — cancel-booking

| Slice | Ready | Waiting | Waits in order | Blocked | Needs verify | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cancel-booking | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 3 |

Result: ready-partial

Run next:

**feat/orders-retry**
Retry a failed refund to the original card.
2 open tasks:
- T5 refund to the original card
- T6 send the mail

Run the whole branch:
`/crav1-build-walk feat/orders-retry`
Run only T5, the first task:
`/crav1-build-walk T5`

Held:
- `feat/orders-currency` (wave 1): T7 choose the currency — open question "Which currency for refunds?" Waiting for the partner.

/crav1-build-tasks builds one task without the walk.

Source: docs/specs/cancel-booking/spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, verify.md
Build map: docs/specs/cancel-booking/build-map.md
```

Held also lists a task whose only wait is an `(after:)` on a task that is not built yet, and the reason is on that line rather than a footer.

Say `full` (`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build full cancel-booking`) for the long form.

```text
Ready now
- `feat/orders-retry` (wave 1): T5 refund to the original card

Waits in order (dependency order)
- T6 send the mail: waits on T5 (recorded).

Needs verify
- T3 short name: no verify.md row.

Done: 3
```

`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`, the tighten-and-plan ready check and `/crav1-build-walk` build it with one shared `walk_ending` script, so for the same ready branches the Run next entries are the same words in all three. `/crav1-build-tasks` reads the full readiness JSON (`--full`) to start the ready tasks. See [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md#the-shared-walk-ending-11560).

a `---` line, with a blank line on each side, stands between two branch blocks so they never run together in a Markdown viewer. A listed task that cannot start yet says why on its line, for example `- T8 Take in develop (waits on T5)`, and when the first listed task cannot start the label is `Run only T#, the first task that can start:`. The plain sentence is used only when the plan step's first sentence is clean: it ends with a full stop, has no colon list, and does not open with a person (`Person A builds ...`). A long line, a sentence or a held question, is cut at a clause end or a word, never on a dangling word such as `the`, and a held question that opens with a heading such as `Client certificate.` shows the question itself. each ready branch is one block with its open tasks listed, `Run the whole branch:` first and `Run only T#, the first task:` second, each command alone on its own line under its label; the reply also ends with `Zoom the map in your browser:` and `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build <slug> open-map`. Before that, since 1.155.0 each ready branch offered its next task, and, when the branch has two or more open tasks, the whole branch as a second entry, built in one run by `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <branch>`. When a whole-branch run is going, or stopped, the ending also has a `Branch runs:` block from the `- Branch run:` status lines in `walk-progress.md`, for example `- feat/orders-retry: running, T5 done, next T6 (log: build-progress/feat--orders-retry.md)`.

every branch block has a description line between the bold branch and `<n> open tasks:`. In order: up to three clean sentences from the plan step (each ends with a full stop, has no colon list, no person leading it and no file or path), about 300 characters at most and cut only at a sentence end, never mid-sentence; else the plan note trimmed to its opening clause, the words before the first `:` or ` — `, with a person lead such as `Person A builds PR 73:` dropped, for example `The orders CI/CD branch, cut from develop after billing-ops.`; else the step's heading in plain words; else one sentence from the open task names, a shared prefix once, for example `Orders CI/CD: infra Bicep, cd pipeline, ci lint and tests, and deploy README.`, about 160 characters. The line is left out only when the branch has no plan step and no usable task name, and a person's name never shows. A held question that ends with `:` or only points to a note, such as `The note docs/notes/x.md, in Open questions, question 5, says:`, shows the quoted question that follows: the `>` blockquote under the bullet, else the text in quotes after the colon, else the first sentence ending in `?`.

## Getting recorded reasons

- `/crav1-review-plan` writes `Reviewed: <date>, P# open: <n>` in `plan.md`, and `/crav1-tighten-plan` lowers the count.
- `/crav1-plan-from-spec` ends a task line with `(after: T1)` when the task needs an earlier one.
- `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` asks which tasks a kept-open question blocks and writes `Blocks: T#`. **None** writes `Blocks: none`. **The whole slice** writes `Blocks: whole slice`. `/crav1-plan-from-spec` writes `Blocks: T#` or `Blocks: none` for a question it parks as a risk.

## Azure Boards

It never reads Azure Boards (ADO). Run [`/crav1-ado-sync`](from-ado-sync-pull-tasks.md) to bring task states back.

## The build map (1.128.0)

The file `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md` is how the work will be built, by branch. A task can name another branch with `(map: feat/cancel-refund)`. `(branch: feat/orders-retry)` does the same when no `(map:)` is set. a `feat/…` name in the sentence, or `committed later on feat/orders-cicd`, does the same when neither mark is set. `from develop` after that name is the base. The plan step's `feat/<slug>-<words>` name is only the fallback. `(step: 1)` links a task to a step when the step text does not. `scripts/build_map.py docs/specs/<slug> --recommend T1` prints the branch on the first line and does not write the file.

Wave 1 can start from a dependency point of view. The heading always says how many can start now, including one branch: `1 branch, 1 can start now`. The short name is the work-item title when `work-item.md` has `task: T1 Turn off pipelines 7 and 24`, otherwise the task text up to the first parenthesis, `, in `, or the end of the sentence. When the task text names a different branch, the row adds `Task text names feat/orders-cicd; built on feat/orders-retry`. When the row is the branch on the task line and the plan step's name differs, the row adds `Plan step names feat/orders-one-commit-cleanup-main; built on feat/orders-host-setup-scripts`. The file and the ready-check ending print one line for it, for example `Loop: feat/orders-x and feat/orders-y wait for each other: T14 on feat/orders-x waits for T13 on feat/orders-y, and T13 on feat/orders-y waits for T12 on feat/orders-x.` Since 1.161.0 the kit offers the fix under that line instead of asking for a hand edit: for example `Recommended fix (say `fix-loop`): T14 and T15 are on feat/orders-x, but they wait for T13 on feat/orders-y, which itself waits for feat/orders-x to merge, so the two branches wait for each other. Build T14 and T15 on feat/orders-y instead, right after T13. Then feat/orders-x holds T9-T12 and merges first, and feat/orders-y runs T13, T14, T15, T16.` Say `fix-loop`, or `fix-loop <n>` for an alternative, confirm the card, and the kit writes the `(map:)` marks, rebuilds the map and shows the loop is gone. Those branches are listed under Blocked, in an `In a loop` group of the flowchart. A branch is always in a later wave than each branch it waits for, unless both are in the same loop. A held line shows the wave, or `in a loop`, never `(blocked)`. The word `build-map` prints the path, each wave's count, and that wave's overlap notes, one line per pair.

The row strikes the short name through and marks it done, with the pull request link, or the branch or commit when there is no pull request: `~~Persist the decision (T1)~~ ✓ done ([PR 12](https://github.com/contoso/orders-api/pull/12))`. the shown task is the plain name and the code in parentheses, for example `Add login page (T3)`. The heading counts done tasks apart from the branches that can start (`1 branch, 1 can start now, 1 done`). A wave whose every task is done is wrapped in a details block, `Wave 1 done (2 tasks)`.

## Zoom the map, or send it (1.162.0)

Say `open-map` to see the whole `build-map.md` as a page in your browser:

`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build orders-api open-map`

The diagram sits in place with zoom on the mouse wheel, drag to pan, and `-`, `+`, `Fit`, `100%` and `Fullscreen` buttons. It works offline: the kit ships Mermaid and marked in `crav1-tasks-ready-to-build/scripts/vendor/`.

To show the map to someone, say `export-map`:

`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build orders-api export-map`

That writes one file, for example `orders-api-build-map-2026-11-15.html`, to your Downloads folder, never into the specs repo. It is about 2.6 MB and opens with a double-click in any browser, offline, with nothing to install.

A done branch says `Waited for:` instead of `Waits for:`, since nothing waits any more.

## When verify.md is behind (1.136.0)

The check reads `verify.md` and does not write it. A task stays done for later tasks when it is ticked, or when its pull request is recorded merged: `(PR n)` and the word merged on the task line, or on the Match `Branch:` line for that task's branch. The check adds a Waiting line when a ticked task is still `Not implemented`, when an older `Next:` line names a ticked task whose own row is not current, or when a merged task is still `Not implemented`. a Verified or Failed row is current, so a fresh verify is never behind, and verify no longer writes a `Next:` line. `task_order.py` lists that task under Needs tick, not under Ready. A verify-only change does not force `not-ready`. This command only writes `build-map.md`. Only the walk's record or `clear --yes` restamps `walk-progress.md`.

a built task whose verify failed is in the Catch up first block as `T6 failed verify: <reason>.`, with `Fix T6:` and `/crav1-fix-build-gaps <slug> T6`, not sent back to verify. Ready branches keep their blocks after the catch-up block and the `---` line, and the result is ready-partial. Questions that are not asked yet stay a `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions <slug>` entry after the branch blocks.

the reason is short: the Verify cell's opening sentence, plus the sentence that names the cause (`... made the asserts stale.`, `... because ...`) when it fits, about 200 characters, cut only at a sentence end. Leading run detail such as `fail at PR 7's tip abc1234: pipeline 6 run 251, 110 failed, 173 passed.` gives way to the next sentence. The full cell stays in `verify.md`, and `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` reads it there. a hold with nobody named says so plainly: `Nobody is named to answer it yet.` for a question, `Nobody is named to give it yet.` for an approval, and `nobody named for 1` on the Waiting line, never `Waiting for not named yet`.

It leads Run next as a `**Catch up first**` block, before the branch blocks and in the same layout: verify.md behind tasks.md, a verify.md row for a T# that is not in tasks.md, and a specs repo ahead of origin. `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec` checks the behind tasks and drops a row for a T# that tasks.md does not have, so the two share one command.

```text
Run next:

**Catch up first**
verify.md is behind for T2 and T45, and it has a row for T44, which is not in tasks.md.

Check T2 and T45 against the spec and remove the T44 row:
`/crav1-verify-build-against-spec orders-api`
Push the specs repo, which is 2 commits ahead of origin:
`git push`

---

**feat/orders-api-record**
...
```

With only the orphan row the label is `Remove the T44 row (it is in verify.md but not in tasks.md):`. Before 1.167.0 the check printed `Waiting: /crav1-verify-build-against-spec orders-api - verify.md is behind tasks.md (T2, T45)` near the bottom.

It does not show that `Next:` line from `verify.md`. `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` still rewrites only `build-map.md`.

## What does not get written

`verify.md` stays with `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`.

`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` keeps the task rules in its skill file and reads a references file only when that case applies: work branches, a sub-branch, promotion, a work item, a plan risk that blocks the slice, or a next line that is not the ready list.

a done task on the build map keeps its own commit: the merge commit in its branch's `build-progress` file, else its own row in `verify.md`. A `Date:` line or another task's row that names a newer commit never replaces it, and with no own commit the mark already on the map stays. Held and ready lines show full task names, and the open-questions entry is `Ask the open questions, which haven't been asked yet:` above `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions <slug>`.

the ready check offers `Continue the build walk on <branch>:` only for your own walk: the walk's claim user in `claims.md` (else the `Run yes:` name in its `build-progress` file) must match `git config user.name`, the same check that makes a claim yours. `Owner: self` in the progress file means whoever ran that walk, so it is never trusted alone. Someone else's walk is a Waiting line instead, `Waiting: T9 to T12 are person B's, built, and wait for PR 82 to merge.`, or `Waiting: T9 to T12 are in progress by person B.` when the pull request is not known. A claimed task that is already built on a branch that is not merged reads `built by <name>, waits for PR <n> to merge` in the Held list, the status and `build-map.md`, not `in progress by <name> since <date>`. A reopened step's entry says why in one plain sentence, which names the changed spec sections or files and the tasks that wait, above an action label, `Finish the reopened /crav1-tighten-spec step:`. A build walk's own files (claims.md, walk-progress.md, build-progress, verify.md and task ticks) never reopen a step. The Catch up first push entry says how far ahead once, in its label `Push the specs repo, which is 2 commits ahead of origin:`, with no sentence repeating it.

a done task's commit is the merge commit from its branch's `merge-pr` step, not the later commit that ticked it. A branch whose tasks are built and whose pull request is open reads `built, waits for PR <n> to merge`, never waiting on its own tasks, and the `Delivers:` and `Tasks:` lines show full names. An unfinished branch walk is the first Run next entry, `Continue the build walk on <branch>:` above `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <branch>`.

a free-text mention such as `(PR 12)` or `(PR 7 merged into develop)` does not mark a task done. Only a tick, or the kit mark `(PR n, merged)` or `(PR n) merged`, does. A task with `(after: T#)` stays held while T#'s pull request is still open, on this check and on the build map, and the held line says `waits for PR <n> to merge`. A task that says `(after: PR 87)`, or whose text says `after PR 87 merges`, stays held until the host says PR 87 is merged. The held line, the build map and the walk ending all say `waits for PR 87 to merge`. When the code repo is not recorded, the check uses the same one-time repo question as 1.177.2. When the host says that pull request is merged, Run next leads with `/crav1-build-walk <slug> T#`. A `--text` read that does not pass `--write-map` does not add a `PR author` line. A merged pull request is still recorded, as in 1.177.2.

## After

`/crav1-build-tasks` builds one task without the walk:

```text
/crav1-build-walk T5 refund to the original card
@docs/specs/<slug>/
```

## Claims and a fresh copy (1.151.0)

If that copy is behind origin, it stops and Run next is `git pull --no-rebase`. A task with an `In progress:` line in `docs/specs/<slug>/claims.md` is held `in progress by <user> since <date>` and is not offered in Run next.

a pull request in the `Merge these PRs, in this order:` list gets no Waiting line of its own. When none of the listed pull requests is yours, Run next leads with `Ask the PR owners to merge, in this order:` and one line per owner. A merge-list line that says `owner not recorded` means neither the kit's records nor the pull request's host named who opened it; the skill asks you once and records your answer with `walk_progress.py pr-author --root <spec-folder> --pr <n> --name "<who>"`, so you never edit a spec file.

A pull request closed without merging gets `Waiting: PR <n> was closed without merging; its tasks are not done.` When no `Code repo:` line or single `docs/system/repos.md` row says where a pull request lives, the reply says `code repo not recorded`; the skill asks you once which repo it is in, records it with `walk_progress.py code-repo --root <spec-folder> --pr <n> --repo <name-or-url>`, and runs the check again. The `Build map:` line ends `(updated)` or `(unchanged, nothing new since the last write)`.

You are asked who opened a pull request only when the host could not say, and the choices include the names the kit already knows, plus `Don't know`. In `build-map.md` each branch box is coloured by its worst task: green done, amber waiting on a pull request or a question, red truly blocked, blue ready or not started, with a legend.

the ready check also reaches Azure DevOps on Windows, where `az` is `az.cmd`. Catch up first says why, for example not signed in, with the command that fixes it under its label, such as `az login`, and then asks you to run the ready check again. The owner question offers the people open questions wait on, never a team or the word other.

A task that waits on a task that can only tick when its own branch's pull request merges is shown as Blocked, a merge deadlock, with `/crav1-tighten-plan` to fix the order. Names like `Admin Person A` or `Person B (Tag)` are cleaned to `Person A` and `Person B`, stored lines too, and the reply ends with a `Recorded:` line naming the files it wrote.

Reference page: [tasks-ready-to-build](reference/skills/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md) · Routes: [Workflow routes](reference/workflow.md)

The run ends as [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md) says: one Run next block with one entry per ready branch, `Waiting:` only when a step is blocked, and `Uncommitted:` when files changed and are not committed.

a task already built on a branch that is not merged is never offered as startable, even when your own claim names it, and older progress files whose header lists only the first task still count every task a done build step names. Tasks that wait on it read `held, waits on PR 21 to merge (T47, recorded)`, and the merge list names only the tasks you claimed as `you added`.

`build-map.md` no longer starts with the sentences naming `open-map` and `export-map`; the heading is followed by the grouping line, such as `One branch per plan step.`, and then the diagram. `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build <slug> open-map` and `export-map` work as before.

that also holds for older progress files whose second task's build step is a plain `build` with `done (T47: ...)` in its result: T47 is built and waits for the merge, the merge list says the pull request ticks both, and dependants wait on that merge.

each branch block in `build-map.md` is easier to scan: `- Tasks:` and `- Waits for:` list one item per nested sub-bullet instead of joining them with `; `, a done task keeps its strike-through and `✓ done (PR 12)` on its own sub-bullet, and `Waits for: none` stays on one line.

the ready check offers `/crav1-build-walk <slug> T#` only when the walk can start that task: both ask the same `task_state.walk_start`.

the ready check and the build map name a task by its text up to the first verify item (`; integration —`, `; contract —`, `; system —`, `; unit —`, or a `(verify: ...)` block), so the checks no longer show in the open-task list or under Run next.
